Senses.Explanation: To divide (分) and to distinguish or separate (別): 'to distinguish' or 'tell apart,' and as a noun, distinguishing. The Chan corpus most often places it in negative constructions: 'do not arouse distinguishing' (不起分別), 'do not distinguish' (莫分別), and 'apart from distinguishing' (離分別). It is paired with 'thinking' (思量)—'thinking and distinguishing' (思量分別, 165 occurrences)—and with 'deluded thought' (妄想), as 'deluded-thought distinguishing' (妄想分別). Dahui says, 'this matter is not what thinking and distinguishing can grasp; now say—when you neither distinguish nor think, what is it?' (是法非思量分別之所能解。且道不分別不思量時是箇甚麼). One passage says, 'because of second-thought distinguishing there are marks; apart from distinguishing there really are no marks' (以第二念分別故有相；若離分別，實無有相). Another says, 'when the distinguishing mind arises, one sees objects existing—this is called ignorance' (分別心起，見有境界，名為無明). A positive use also occurs: the Platform Record preserves the line, 'well able to distinguish the marks of all things, yet unmoved from the first principle' (能善分別諸法相，於第一義而不動). Attested collocations include 'the distinguishing mind' (分別心, 88 occurrences), 'without distinguishing' (無分別, 436), 'arouse or not arouse distinguishing' (起／不起分別), 'thinking and distinguishing' (思量分別), and 'deluded-thought distinguishing' (妄想分別). The entry records these uses without replacing 'distinguish' with an abstract theory.
Senses.Note: The Chan-record deployment is predominantly "the distinguishing to be dropped" (不起／莫／離分別, "do not arouse / do not / apart from distinguishing," paired with "thinking" (思量) and "deluded thought" (妄想)), while the Platform Sutra preserves a positive "well able to distinguish the marks of all things" (善分別諸法相). The Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄) witness by Yongming Yanshou (永明延壽) comes from expository prose and supplies the explicit equation that the arising of the distinguishing mind (分別心) is called ignorance (無明). Compare "thinking" (思量), "deluded thought" (妄想), and "the distinguishing mind" (分別心).

Occurrences.Kwic: 是法非思量分別之所能解。且道不分別不思量時是箇甚麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), by Dahui Zonggao, his upper-hall address (上堂) — he abruptly takes the staff and strikes it down once (驀拈拄杖卓一下), then says this; distinguishing (分別) paired with thinking (思量) as what cannot reach "this matter" (是法).

Occurrences.Kwic: 分別心起。見有境界。名為無明。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Records of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄), by Yongming Yanshou (永明延壽). The passage equates the arising of the distinguishing mind (分別心) with seeing objects as existing (見有境界), and names that ignorance (無明). It is cited only for this explicit equation.
